- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >+5% from prior), often followed by correction; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and model is rising, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overreaction.  
- Model often overestimates mean reversion in short-term (1–3 days) after volatility; apply slight downward bias (–0.5% to –1.5%) for next 3–5 days.  
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 70), model tends to ignore it; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period prices; reduce final 5–7 days by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
